title: Nonsingular systems of equations over arbitrary groups
main_claim: Howie's conjecture: for any group G and words w_1..w_m in G*F_n whose exponent-sum matrix has rational rank m, G embeds in (G*F_n)/<<w_1..w_m>>.
coverage: Read every mathematical section in full: fixed-space, phase, planar and kernel. (1) Phase section: I checked that the trace is faithful and normal for uncountable G. I checked the subadditivity proof (derivative identity, D^{1/2} positivity trick, one-sided smoothing so f'<=1 and f_eps->h at the cut). I checked the weighted-cycle formula, including the scalar identity sum_j h(zeta^j lambda)=(a-1)/2+h(lambda^a) and the conjugation of the diagonal entries of T^a. (2) Planar proposition: p_i=m_i follows from row rank. Euler characteristic 2-q=2K-b. The phase-distribution graph argument holds. I verified JSJ=S^{-1} from the slot-convention table. SJ is a trace-zero involution, so ell(SJ)=b/2. On V_{j,+}, J's block is X_i^{-s} and the signed counts are -a_ij. J conjugates JTheta to its inverse, giving f>=2K and the bound ell(SJ)+ell(JTheta)<=3b/2-K. The boundary-side computation also gives exactly 3b/2-K + tau(h(L(r^{-1}))), and the eps->0 limit is handled correctly. (3) Fixed-space theorem: I checked the choice of nested nonzero minors and that l_j<=d_j. Rational cohomology of U(d) has primitive, block-compatible generators; the Serre spectral sequence and edge-map argument is valid. The incidence manifold R(d,l) is oriented and has codimension l^2. The leading term e_1...e_l is forced by degree. I verified that c_{d,l}!=0 via transversality at W0=I+(-I), where [T,W0]W0^{-1}=2T. The pullback formula follows from primitivity and inversion. Shorter terms vanish because the top-degree monomial needs every generator. Grouping by degree gives the product of nested minors. (4) Kernel section: the punctured-disk map from a normal-closure expression is valid. The PL level arcs of the circle maps are disjoint and v is constant near them. Endpoint signs are opposite. The surfaces are planar, and the innermost-first filling works by minimality. The remark extending to infinite systems is correct. Numerics (python): ell(UV)<=ell(U)+ell(V) held in 20k random trials (dimension 1-5, maximum violation 4e-16). For a nontrivial fixed-space instance (k=2, one variable with blocks (+,+,-), random P in U(6)), optimization found X with a 2-dimensional fixed space to 1e-26 accuracy. The only flaws are harmless wording slips, e.g. 'degree less than l^2' where the actual point is that the monomial has fewer generators than needed for top degree.
